metadata.note: The Chicago, Burlington & Quincy's namesake Chicago-Galesburg-Quincy line and its Zephyr streamliners, the historical predecessor of Amtrak's Carl Sandburg and Illinois Zephyr. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.source: Wikipedia (Chicago Burlington and Quincy Railroad, Zephyr, Illinois Zephyr and Carl Sandburg), american-rails.com
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The CB&Q's namesake Illinois main line. Its ancestor the Aurora Branch was chartered Feb 12 1849, renamed the Chicago & Aurora in 1852, reached Galesburg in 1854, and took the Chicago, Burlington & Quincy name in 1856. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: The Burlington became famous for its Zephyr streamliners, beginning with the Pioneer Zephyr - America's first diesel-powered streamlined passenger train - and its celebrated dawn-to-dusk Denver-Chicago run of May 26 1934; a large Zephyr fleet followed over Burlington lines. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable

segments.note: CB&Q merged into Burlington Northern in 1970; Amtrak took over May 1 1971. The corridor now carries Amtrak's Illinois Zephyr and Carl Sandburg - see amtrak.geojson. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
